team.name: dream-team
team.description: Stack-agnostic multi-agent development team for Claude Code. Invoke with /team <task>.

modelRouting._comment: The model for each Agent call: the cell for its workflow and call (by the task's Complexity where the cell is low/medium/high), one tier up when the orchestrator judged the run hard, then raised to the role's floor and capped at the session model; the ceiling wins over the floor. ceiling = the session model, passed by omitting model, which is why every agent file declares model: inherit. A call key's suffix marks a second kind of call to one role (researcher-explorer:wide = the wide research pass, reviewer:final = the review of the whole diff); its floor is the role's. Layout is read line by line: each workflow opens on its own line, one call per line, a low/medium/high object inline.

budgets._comment: Checked at four characters to one token; no tokenizer is available to the skills that read this. A file listed in overrides is measured against its own number instead of the default for its class.

classification._comment: subset = a reader needs part of it, so it becomes an index at this path plus a sibling directory of topics. whole = every reader needs all of it, so it stays one file and is cut, never split.

CAPABILITIES.md.note: Describes this machine, not this repository: which optional capabilities are installed and how the team may use them. Rewritten by every /team-setup run. Absent or empty means the team runs with none, which is a supported state.

hooks.purpose: Sticky team mode: while the marker file exists, every user prompt is routed back through the /team orchestrator, surviving model switches, pauses, compaction and restarts.
hooks.requires: a bash shell (Git Bash or WSL on Windows); without one the hook exits quietly and sticky mode is simply unavailable

pluginPolicy.consent: Every plugin in this list is optional and is installed only after the user agrees to that specific plugin. /team-setup reports what is missing and asks before installing anything. /team and the subagents never install, enable or disable a plugin.
pluginPolicy.degradation: The team must produce the same quality of work with none of these installed. A capability is an accelerator, never a prerequisite. An agent that cannot see a capability proceeds without it and never tells the user something was impossible because a plugin was absent.
pluginPolicy.brokering: Subagents run with the tool list in their own frontmatter, which does not include tools contributed by plugins. By default the orchestrator uses a capability itself and passes the result into the handoff. A team owner who wants an agent to call a capability directly must add that capability's tools to the agent's frontmatter; /team-setup reports which agents would need that and never edits them.
pluginPolicy.verification: Install identifiers below were confirmed against the official marketplace listing and the vendors' own installation instructions in September 2026. Re-check before relying on one; /team-setup reports what is actually installed rather than trusting this file.

plugins.name: context7
plugins.alternativeInstall: claude mcp add --scope user context7 -- npx -y @upstash/context7-mcp
plugins.useWhen: The task depends on a third-party library or framework and the exact current signature, option name, or version-specific behaviour is not visible in this repository. Look it up before designing or writing the call, not after it fails.
plugins.neverUseFor: Anything about this project's own code, conventions or commands — those come from .claude/knowledge/ and the repository itself. Fetched documentation never overrides an observed project convention; when they disagree, the repository wins and the disagreement is reported.

plugins.name: claude-mem
plugins.install: /plugin marketplace add thedotmack/claude-mem, then /plugin install claude-mem
plugins.detect: a tool or command whose name contains "mem", contributed by this plugin
plugins.useWhen: At preflight, to recall the user's standing preferences and what earlier sessions concluded about this project. Treat every recollection as a hint to verify, never as a fact.
plugins.neverUseFor: Storing the team's own learnings. LEARNINGS.md stays the team's one inbox of project traps on their way to becoming rules: it is reviewable, project-scoped and lives beside the code. Never let a recollection outrank the repository or the knowledge files.

plugins.name: claude-md-management
plugins.detect: a command for revising the project instruction file, contributed by this plugin
plugins.useWhen: At the docs-sync step of a run that changed a documented rule or created a new obligation: propose the instruction-file update through this capability and let the user approve the diff.
plugins.neverUseFor: Editing project instruction files silently or in the middle of a run, and regenerating PROJECT-RULES.md — that belongs to the knowledge generator, which reads the instruction file rather than writing it.

plugins.name: chrome-devtools-mcp
plugins.detect: a tool for navigating, inspecting or screenshotting a live browser page
plugins.useWhen: A run changed something a person sees and the result can be observed by loading the running application: the Tester needs a check against real rendering, the Reviewer needs to confirm the change actually appears, or a diagnosis needs the real console or network behaviour.
plugins.neverUseFor: Projects with no user interface; starting a server or opening a page without the user agreeing first; and never as a substitute for a test — a screenshot is evidence, not coverage.

plugins.name: playwright
plugins.marketplace: (not published as a marketplace plugin as of September 2026)
plugins.detect: a tool for driving a browser through structured page data
plugins.useWhen: Same as the other browser-control entry. Install at most one of the two: two browser drivers competing for the same page waste context and produce contradictory observations.
plugins.neverUseFor: Same exclusions as the other browser-control entry.

servicePolicy.consent: A service sends data off this machine, so having its credential is not consent. /team-setup fix asks per service and per provider, naming what is sent and who receives it, and records the answer in .claude-tracking/.service-consent (machine-local, never committed) as {name}=granted {provider} {date} or {name}=declined {date}; the last line for a service wins. Consent to one provider is not consent to another, because the recipients differ. The client refuses to send anything without a granted line, and uses only the credential, endpoint and model of the provider that line names.
servicePolicy.egress: Only the fields named in an entry's dataSent ever leave the machine. Code, diffs, knowledge files, task files and paths never do.
servicePolicy.degradation: Same as pluginPolicy.degradation: without the service, or when it is slow or failing, the team does the same work the same way, and no output mentions the service's absence.
servicePolicy.brokering: Only the orchestrator calls a service, and only through the entry's script. Subagents never do.
servicePolicy.modes: shadow = ask and log, never act on the answer. act = the answer may influence a decision within the rules skills/team/SKILL.md gives. The mode is the team's policy, set here, not per machine.

services.name: jev
services.credentialNote: Each provider's credential names an environment variable in the environment Claude Code runs in. The user sets it; the team never writes it anywhere.
services.keySetup: Put the key in the env block of your user settings, ~/.claude/settings.json: "env": { "{credential}": "<key>" }. Claude Code passes it to every shell it starts, on every OS. A variable exported from your shell profile, or set with setx on Windows, works too. Never put it in the project's .claude/settings.json, which is committed, and never paste it into the chat. Restart Claude Code, then run /team-setup again.

typesafe.keyUrlNote: TypeSafe's documentation names no sign-up or key page, and none was confirmed when this entry was written. Say so, and point the user there to start.
typesafe.retention: TypeSafe does not train on customer data. Zero retention is offered to enterprise customers only; otherwise its data processing agreement applies.

openrouter.recipients: OpenRouter, which passes the request to TypeSafe AI: two companies receive the text
openrouter.retention: OpenRouter's own privacy terms apply on top of TypeSafe's. Its retention for this endpoint was not confirmed when this entry was written; say so and let the user check before agreeing.

services.dataSent: The user's task text as typed, cut to 8000 characters, and one fixed question set from templates/jev. Nothing else.
services.detect: the chosen provider's credential is set, consent names that provider, and bash tools/jev-decide.sh probe {provider} prints a response
services.useWhen: Step 0 workflow selection, and the difficulty of a Bug Fix or Small Change task, as skills/team/SKILL.md → Decision routing describes.
services.neverUseFor: Anything security-relevant, any decision that needs the code, review verdicts, Brainstorm quorum, skipping or softening a gate, and sending anything beyond dataSent.

updateCheck._comment: Optional, off by default. /team-setup fix asks and records update-check=granted|declined {date} in .claude-tracking/.service-consent; the client sends nothing without a granted line. /team runs the client once at the start of a new run; it asks source at most once per intervalHours and caches the answer in .claude-tracking/.update-check. The team never updates itself: instructions is shown to the user verbatim.
updateCheck.dataSent: One HTTPS GET of a public file. No task text, code or paths; GitHub sees the machine's IP address and the time of the request.
updateCheck.instructions: From the project root, in bash: git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/dm-23/dream-team.git /tmp/dream-team && cp -r /tmp/dream-team/. .claude/ && rm -rf .claude/.git /tmp/dream-team — then reopen the session, run /team-setup check, and run /team resume to continue the parked run.

checks.runFrom: the team root: this repository, or .claude/ in a project the team is deployed into
checks.note: "hook" is deliberately absent from this pattern: it is a Claude Code harness term the team must be able to name. React's hooks are caught by useState/useEffect instead.
checks.stackNeutralityLint: grep -n -i -E "\b(go|golang|python|java|c#|csharp|dotnet|typescript|javascript|node|react|angular|vue|redux|usestate|useeffect|selector|slice|controller|mediatr|cqrs|linq|dbcontext|prisma|sqlalchemy|xunit|nunit|jest|vitest|pytest|npm|pip|nuget|cargo|csproj|axios|fetch|swagger|openapi|gofmt|eslint|prettier|nullable|eager.?load|n\+1|re-?render|functional component|any types|router)\b" agents/*.md skills/*/SKILL.md README.md
checks.routingSummaryReport: bash .claude/checks/summarize-routing.sh — run from the project root; prints the decision-routing shadow numbers from every run's routing.log
checks.knowledgeIntegrityArgs: <backup-dir> <knowledge-dir>, in that order; exit 0 means every guarantee held
checks.knowledgeIntegrityRunFrom: the project root, not .claude/: both arguments are project-root-relative, so prefix the script path with .claude/ — bash .claude/checks/verify-knowledge-integrity.sh .claude-tracking/knowledge-backup-<stamp> .claude/knowledge
checks.learningsInboxArgs: <knowledge-dir>; exit 0 = inbox clean, 1 = /generate-knowledge all is due, 2 = could not read what it needs
checks.learningsInboxRunFrom: the project root, not .claude/: the argument is project-root-relative, so prefix the script path with .claude/ — bash .claude/checks/verify-learnings-inbox.sh .claude/knowledge
